name: Cuneus Equitum Catafractariorum

abilities.name: Wedge
abilities.text: The unit moves into a wedge-shaped attack formation.

abilities.name: Trample
abilities.text: Charges are more effective for an extended time.

attributes.name: Disciplined
attributes.text: This unit does not suffer a morale penalty when the general dies. It can also rally after routing more often.

attributes.name: Scare (everyone)
attributes.text: This unit frightens all enemy units.

attributes.name: Immune to Fear
attributes.text: This unit is immune to the fear effects of scary units.

short: Cuneus equitum - a spearhead, a wedge of horsemen, it is a wedge-shaped battle formation used to concentrate the onslaught and break through the enemy formation. It is assumed that the cunei were separated by Constantine I from the equites which were formed under Diocletian on the basis of the old cavalry units. The fact that several units of cuneus have received the status of Comitatenses (according to Notita Dignitatum), can testify about high combat efficiency of these units. Most likely these units were armed with contus (Ancient Greek kontos, «bear spear»; Latin contus) - a huge spear. The term Cataphractarii comes from the Greek word kataphraktos, formed from the Greek origins of the words kata, preposition, and phraktos («covered, protected»), which can be translated as «completely covered, protected» or «covered on all sides». In the Roman army, the first cataphractarian units appeared under Emperor Hadrian (117-138 AD). They were organized on the example of the Sarmatian cavalry and wore scaled metal or combined armor, chain mail, and composite helmets. The composite armor included a thighplate, metal or leather handcuffs and greaves. With no shields, cataphractarii fought with long spears (contus) held with both hands. Despite doubts about the effectiveness of the cataphractarii on the battlefield, the large number of their units indicates that cataphractarii had an important place in military operations during the Late Roman Empire.
history: Having faced the deadly Parthian cataphracts at Carrhae, come off worse, and then struggled against the awesome crushing strength of the Sarmatian lancers, it wasn't long before the Roman army was tailoring its own cavalry to match, despite resisting the idea for some time. Gradually, Rome began to integrate its own versions, the catafractarii and clibinarii, into the Legions. They were probably first fielded during the reign of the Emperor Hadrian, as an auxiliary force of Gauls and Pannonians. However, despite their general success, it was the 4th century AD before catafractarii became a permanent addition to the ranks, possibly due to Macrinus' catastrophic defeat at Nisibis in AD217, by the Parthians. Covered head-to-foot in scale or mail armour, and armed with lances, it is clear that the 'iron horsemen' were the forerunners to the more familiar knights of the Medieval age.
strengths: Very low damage and armour penetration
